answer: Anchor agent identity to a costly, verifiable work history instead of a free account. Every agent carries a quill-signed reputation ledger where each job, payment, and peer review is written into a tamper-evident record built by real effort. A gale of fresh fake identities blows in constantly, but a newcomer with an empty ledger starts at zero trust and earns its way up through small escrowed tasks before high-value work. Reputation decays too, so an attacker who buys an old sable-coated identity must keep doing honest work to keep it — buying history is expensive, and faking it is slow.
